description: Lebanese Arabizi vocabulary seeds per sector. Used by corpus annotation team to author Arabizi complaints faster. Process: write seed → human edits to natural Lebanese Arabizi → add to corpus. DO NOT use raw seeds as corpus without human review.
changelog: 1.7.0 (2026-05-22): V20b comprehensive OOV absorption — 43 new term_metadata entries (civic infrastructure, weather, governance, discourse) + 6 variant-form patches. Reviewer: SYSTEM-V20b.

common_substitutions.ح: 7  — ALWAYS use 7; never use plain h for this letter
common_substitutions.خ: 5  — preferred in standalone seeds and word-initial position (5atar, 5tr). kh is acceptable mid-word only (dakhlet, mekshouf, dukhaan). NEVER use both forms for the same word in the same seed list
common_substitutions.ق: 2  — preferred (ma2tou3, tari2, 7a2). q is acceptable in formal/MSA loanwords only
common_substitutions.ص: s or S  — lowercase s is standard; capital S is optional for disambiguation
common_substitutions.ط: t  — context usually distinguishes from ت
common_substitutions.ء / أ / إ / ئ: 2  — use for glottal stop in any position
common_substitutions.ه: h  — plain h is correct ONLY for ه, not for ح

transliteration_rules.خطر_danger: ALWAYS write 5atar (not khatar) in seed keywords. kh form only in sample complaints where mid-word position makes 5 awkward
transliteration_rules.حفرة_pothole: Prefer 7ofra or 7afra in authored seeds. Keep hofra as a low-confidence wild variant because real users omit 7; never use hafra or hufra.
transliteration_rules.prepositions: Avoid stacking more than two locational particles (fi/bi/3al) in a row. Use 3al as the default for 'on/at'; fi for 'inside/in a place'; bi for 'in/at' with proper nouns
transliteration_rules.verb_agreement: Match verb number to subject: seyyarat (plural) → 2adroo / 2adret, not 2adra (singular feminine)
transliteration_rules.ma_fi_vs_ma_fiye: ma fi = ما في (there is no / there isn't). ma fiye = ما فيّي (I cannot). Choose the correct form based on intended meaning
transliteration_rules.marker_chars_in_seeds: Single-word seeds (e.g. jora, seyle, nnar) may not contain a marker character (3/7/2/5) — this is expected and does not make them invalid. The quality gate requiring at least one marker applies to full corpus REPORTS, not individual seed words. Short seeds without markers are fine as lookup tokens; the full complaint built from them must contain at least one marker character.

common_connectors.الـ: l- (most common) or el- or al-
common_connectors.خطر: 5atar  (preferred in seeds); 5tr  (abbreviated panic form); khatar  (acceptable mid-word only)

lexicon_policy.goal: High-precision Lebanese municipal incident Arabizi seeds, not an exhaustive slang dictionary.
lexicon_policy.acceptance_rule: Keep a seed only if it is Lebanese-plausible, useful for municipal incident reports, and either observed in corpus, confirmed by a Lebanese speaker, or anchored by public local usage.
lexicon_policy.do_not_use_as_final_labels: The keys in issue_type_keywords must match annotation issue types; old local names live only in issue_type_aliases.
lexicon_policy.noise_handling: Do not enumerate every repeated-character typo. Normalizer should collapse repeated trailing letters/digits, e.g. 5tr444444 -> 5tr.
lexicon_policy.adaptive_oov_policy: Unknown meaningful Arabizi terms must be logged to data/corpus/arabizi_oov_review_queue_v1.csv and reviewed before vocabulary promotion. The fixed lexicon remains high-precision; raw text models and HITL handle long-tail language.

source_notes.jora_joura: Public Lebanese pothole usage is anchored by the Ensa Joura road initiative and common local usage; keep jora/joura/joora as high-value variants.
source_notes.balou3a_drain: Lebanese drain usage is anchored by public Lebanese Arabic learning references that transliterate بالوعة as Balou3a; use balou3a/balo3a, not balioa.
source_notes.may_water: Production v1.5.1 treats may/maye as the trusted Lebanese water form. miye and mayye are not active WATER keywords after the correction pass; they remain stoplist/candidate-only items pending native sign-off because they caused false confidence in v1.5.0.
source_notes.kahraba: kahraba/kahrabe variants are common Lebanese Arabic for electricity; keep both in electricity contexts.
source_notes.code_switching: Lebanese reports may code-switch Arabic, Arabizi, French, and English; corpus reports should preserve natural mixing rather than over-normalizing away real usage.
source_notes.kahrabe_variant: kahraba/kahrabe are both attested Lebanese Arabic forms for electricity. v1.4.0 documented this in source_notes but failed to include kahrabe in actual issue_type_keywords. v1.5.0 adds kahrabe forms to ELECTRICITY keywords.
source_notes.dialect_coverage: v1.5.1 keeps regional coverage conservative: darb (path/road — Beqaa/South), bala2a (drain — South Lebanon), wadi (watercourse — mountain/Beqaa flash-flood context), and khadra (water channel — Tripoli/North). mayye and 3ain are not active production water keywords pending native sign-off.

m7arrak.arabizi_note: Canonical form using 7 for ح (m7arrak = محرّك, live/energised wire). Variant mcharrak (ch for ح) is attested in corpus; both are accepted. Seeds use both; m7arrak is the canonical spelling.

transformateur.arabizi_note: French loanword widely used in Lebanese vernacular for transformer (محوّل). Maps to ELECTRICITY/TRANSFORMER_FAULT, not EXPOSED_WIRE.

ghare2.arabizi_note: غارق — flooded/submerged. Standard Lebanese Arabic. Use with tari2/share3 for FLOODING/road_flooded context.

7eet.arabizi_note: Variant spelling of 7iit (حيط = wall). 7eet is a common phonetic alternative; both forms are accepted in seeds.

tita3abba.arabizi_note: تتعبّى — fills up (feminine/inanimate). Context-dependent: in WASTE means bin filling without collection (garbage_not_collected); in FLOODING means drain backing up (blocked_drain, via tit3abba). Disambiguation by sector.
tita3abba.context_disambiguation: FLOODING/blocked_drain uses tit3abba (existing seed); WASTE/garbage_not_collected uses tita3abba

nkesh.arabizi_note: إنكاش — inert construction/demolition debris; WASTE/ILLEGAL_DUMP routing candidate in CB

ta7dir.arabizi_note: warning/caution (تحذير); isharet ta7dir = warning signs; ROADS/FLOODING support term

kasaret.arabizi_note: كسرت — broke/cracked (feminine past tense). Deferred to Batch 002 (NEEDS_MORE_EXAMPLES from OOV queue). Do not promote until ≥3 further corpus examples. Tentative sector: ROADS/pothole or ROADS/road_collapse.

zibele.arabizi_note: زبالة — vowelised form of zbele (garbage/waste). Both forms are attested in Lebanese Arabizi; zbele is the compressed form, zibele is the fuller vowelised form. Both must appear in all WASTE issue type keywords.

7ufra.arabizi_note: حفرة — pothole. Variant of 7ofra / 7afra with ু-vowel. 7ufra was observed in Batch 002 corpus (RPT-B001-066/067/068) but was absent from vocabulary, causing low hit rates. 7ofra is canonical; 7ufra, hofra are accepted variants.

moulid.arabizi_note: موليد / مولّد — generator (informal Lebanese). moulid kharban = generator broken; moulid 3atlan = generator down. muwalid is the rural/Beqaa variant spelling. Maps to ELECTRICITY/transformer_fault when the context is power from a generator, not grid electricity.

sa32.arabizi_note: صاعق — electrocution / electric shock. sa32 is already in HIGH_RISK_HINTS (the authoritative danger list). It must ALSO appear in ELECTRICITY/exposed_wire and SAFETY/exposed_hazard so the keyword lookup confirms the sector. sa3q is an alternative Arabizi spelling of the same word.

nar.arabizi_note: نار — fire. Variant of the emphatic nnar (doubled-n expresses urgency). nar is standard Lebanese Arabic; nnar is the Arabizi panic/emphasis form. Both must appear in SAFETY/fire keywords. 7ari2a (حريقة) is the formal term for a fire incident.

kahrabe.arabizi_note: كهربا — variant of kahraba (electricity). Both forms are common in Lebanese; kahrabe tends to appear in certain Beirut neighbourhoods and older speakers. Documented in source_notes since v1.4.0 but was missing from actual issue_type_keywords; now added to power_outage and exposed_wire.

sayel.arabizi_note: سايل — flowing, running (Lebanese dialect present-participle). sayel l miye = the water is flowing/running (onto the street). Disambiguation: in FLOODING context means water overflow; in WATER/pipe_leak context means pipe running/leaking. Most common in standing_water and flash_flood contexts.

mayye.arabizi_note: miye is the Lebanese dialectal form for ميّه (water); false_friend: miye=100 (مية) in formal Arabic; miye mat3a = water is cut (WATER/WATER_CUT status phrase); must not route on miye alone

darb.arabizi_note: درب — path / lane / small road. Beqaa and South Lebanon dialect word for a small road or lane, equivalent to Beirut's sekke or zuqaq. darb meksour = road damaged; darb ma2tou3 = road blocked. Should be accepted in ROADS keywords alongside tari2/share3/sekke.

panne.arabizi_note: French loanword: panne = breakdown/outage. panne de courant = power outage. Extremely common in Lebanese mixed-language reports (code-switching Arabic + French). Maps to ELECTRICITY/power_outage.

bala2a.arabizi_note: بالوعة — drain. South Lebanon / Bekaa dialect variant of balou3a/balo3a. bala2a msdoude = drain blocked. Phonetic shift: 3 → 2 in the final syllable. Both bala2a and balou3a should be accepted in FLOODING/blocked_drain.

shar2ata.arabizi_note: شرقطة — Lebanese colloquial word for electric shock / electrocution. More colloquial and specific than sa32 (صاعقة), which is the MSA form. shar2ata is the word Beirut residents use when describing getting shocked by a live wire. Maps to ELECTRICITY/exposed_wire. sa32 is retained in HIGH_RISK_HINTS (MSA form) but shar2ata is the primary seed for keyword lookup.

nab3.arabizi_note: نبع — spring / water source. Lebanese word for a natural water spring. nab3 jefef = the spring dried up; nab3 meksouf = source exposed (broken). Use in WATER/no_supply for rural/Beqaa contexts where municipal water comes from natural springs. beer may = water well, also maps here.

ri7a_besh3a.arabizi_note: ريحة بشعة / ريحة مش طيبة — bad/ugly/foul smell. CORRECT replacement for the erroneous 'khafer' (which does not exist in Lebanese Arabic). In WASTE context ri7a besh3a confirms garbage or sewage overflow. Variant forms: ri7a bish3a, ri7a mesh taybe, ri7a mish taybe, ri7a msh mni7a, ri7a msh taybe, ri7et zbele besh3a.

beer_may.arabizi_note: بئر مي — water well. Lebanese compound: beer (بئر = well) + may (مي = water). beer may jfef = the water well dried up. Maps to WATER/no_supply. Common in rural areas and older Beirut neighbourhoods.

2at3a.arabizi_note: قطعة — cut (adjective, feminine). The CORRECT Lebanese Arabizi adjective for 'cut off'. may 2at3a = water cut. kahraba 2at3a = power cut. REPLACES the erroneous 'mat3a' which was mistakenly added in v1.5.0. Also accepted: 2ata3et (verb past tense, already in keywords).

mat3a.arabizi_note: مقطوعة — feminine adj. for cut-off/absent; kahraba mat3a=power cut, miye mat3a=water cut; protected phrase combos in PC; do not route mat3a alone

byiji.arabizi_note: بيجي — 3sg masc present 'comes/will come'; ma 7ada byiji = nobody comes; complaint discourse verb

t2a3.arabizi_note: تقع — falls/drops; bi terji3 t2a3 = keeps falling in (pothole); 2=ء emphatic qaf; ROADS pothole damage signal

terji3.arabizi_note: ترجع — returns/goes back; bi terji3 t2a3 = comes back and falls in; recurring issue discourse marker

titrakam.arabizi_note: تتراكم — accumulates/piles up; zbele 3am titrakam = garbage accumulating; used for WASTE and FLOODING buildup

tirfa3.arabizi_note: ترفع — rises/goes up; miye 3am tirfa3 = water is rising; FLOODING support when paired with water vocab

imbere7.arabizi_note: إمبارح — yesterday (Lebanese); uniquely Lebanese/Levantine colloquial (cf. formal Arabic ams); 7=ح

ghayet.arabizi_note: غاية — extreme/for so long; ghayet min l zaman = for way too long; Lebanese degree/duration idiom in complaint discourse

zaman.arabizi_note: زمان — a long time; men zaman = for a long time/since forever; common unresolved-issue discourse marker

khafer.arabizi_note: خفر — putrid/foul smell emanating from waste; WASTE/OVERFLOWING_BIN signal; 5=خ alternative Arabizi encoding; khafer ktir = very foul smell

bada.arabizi_note: بدا — wants/is going to (3sg masc Lebanese future/desire); ma bada 7ada yiji = nobody comes; common complaint discourse modal verb

la2.arabizi_note: لأ — no (Lebanese); la2 is the Arabizi negation response

khalas.arabizi_note: خلص — done/finished/enough; khalas mish mnekhdo = we're done waiting

leh.arabizi_note: ليش — why; leh mish bi tishtaghal = why isn't it working

ba3ed.arabizi_note: بعد — after/still; ba3ed mat3a = still cut off

badde.arabizi_note: بدي — I want/I need (1sg Lebanese); badde 7all = I need a solution

hayde.arabizi_note: هيدي — this (fem. demonstrative Lebanese); hayde l moshkle = this problem

lezim.arabizi_note: لازم — must/necessary; lezim yiji 7ada = someone must come

ysir.arabizi_note: يصير — it's possible/happens; ysir ykun = it could be

ghalat.arabizi_note: غلط — wrong/mistake; hada ghalat = this is wrong

aal.arabizi_note: قال — said/they said; aal 3anna = they said about us

aktar.arabizi_note: أكتر — more/most; aktar min sene = more than a year

balad.arabizi_note: بلد — country/town/municipality; baladiye l balad = the town municipality

3alam.arabizi_note: عالم — people/world; l 3alam = the people; common in complaints

bet.arabizi_note: بيت — house/home; bet = house (short form); context: near my house

mnel.arabizi_note: من ال — from the (contracted Lebanese); mnel share3 = from the road

walla.arabizi_note: والله — by God (discourse particle); walla ma 3arif = I honestly don't know

tab.arabizi_note: طيب — okay then/well (discourse); tab shu byisawwou = so what are they doing

habibi.arabizi_note: حبيبي — dear/friend (Lebanese address term); used in complaint framing

z3elet.arabizi_note: زعل — upset/angry; z3elet ktir = very upset; high-frequency complaint verb

meshe.arabizi_note: مشي — went/walked/worked; meshe = it worked (passed); ma meshe = didn't work

kenet.arabizi_note: كانت — was (3sg fem past); kenet mat3a = it was cut off

tkoun.arabizi_note: تكون — to be (subjunctive); lazem tkoun = it should be

jem3a.arabizi_note: جماعة — group/guys/crew; jem3a = the team/guys (civic workers reference)

khaye.arabizi_note: خيّ — brother (Lebanese address); used in complaint openers

haram.arabizi_note: حرام — shame/forbidden; haram 3enna = a shame upon us; complaint expression

balat.arabizi_note: بلاط — pavement/tiles; balat l share3 = road paving; ROADS context

t3ebet.arabizi_note: تعبت — exhausted/tired; t3ebet min l moshkle = I'm tired of this problem

wel.arabizi_note: وال — and the (contracted Lebanese); wel baladiye = and the municipality

thawra.arabizi_note: ثورة — revolution; thawra context in civic frustration; 2019 Lebanon protests ref

3atal.arabizi_note: Breakdown/outage variants — عطل; all contain digit markers 3 or 6

zeft.arabizi_note: Asphalt/bitumen — زفت; Lebanese road infrastructure term

silk_el_kahraba.arabizi_note: Electrical wire — سلك; silk/sulk el kahraba = electrical wire

fayadan.arabizi_note: Flood overflow variants — فيضان; common FLOODING sector term

matar.arabizi_note: Rain variants — مطر; matar ktir = heavy rain; FLOODING context

sakef.arabizi_note: Ceiling/roof variants — سقف; sakef 3am yinzer = ceiling cracking

mish_neg.note: Lebanese negation 'not/isn't' — mish/mesh/mich variants. mish/msh already in STOPWORDS; adding extended family for coverage.

mabada_neg.note: Lebanese 'won't/never/hasn't ever been' — mabada family (50+ conjugated forms).

mab2a_neg.note: Lebanese 'won't become/not going to be anymore' — mab2a (2=ء/ق).

bala_neg.note: Lebanese 'without' — bala/bla. 'bla' already in STOPWORDS; adding extended forms.

ana_pronoun.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'I/me' (first-person pronoun). Connector/filler in civic tweet reports.

bas_connector.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'just/only/enough' (discourse particle). Single-s variant of 'bass' already in STOPWORDS.

eno_connector.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'that/that-it' (subordinating conjunction). Variants enno/inno are phonological spelling differences.

hek_demonstrative.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'like this / so / in this way' (demonstrative). High civic co-occurrence — used to describe road/infrastructure state.

hal_demonstrative.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'this / the' (determinative article/prefix before nouns). Very high frequency in civic descriptive sentences.

hada_demonstrative.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'this / someone' (proximal demonstrative pronoun). Appears in civic descriptions: 'hada l-maw2if' = 'this situation'.

chou_question.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'what' (interrogative). Variant shu shares the same root; both OOV vs current vocab.

kif_question.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'how' (interrogative). Frequent in civic complaints: 'kif badna n3ish' = 'how are we to live'.

eza_conditional.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'if' (conditional conjunction). Variants eza/iza both confirmed OOV with civic_ratio ~0.87.

chi_indefinite.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'thing/something' (indefinite pronoun). Note: 'shi' is already in STOPWORDS; 'chi' is the French-influenced spelling.

ma3_preposition.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'with' (preposition). Civic use: 'ma3 kell hayde' = 'with all this'. civic_ratio=0.867.

hala2_temporal.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'now' (temporal marker). Used in civic urgency statements. Arabizi digit '2' = ء/glottal stop.

ba2a_discourse.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'then/so/already' (discourse marker). civic_ratio=0.60; used in complaint conclusions. '2' = glottal stop.

masdoud.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'blocked/closed' (adj). tari2 masdoud = road blocked; biar masdoud = manhole blocked; msakkar/sakker also used. Corpus: cr=0.42, freq=12.

jisr.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'bridge' (noun). jisr meksour = broken bridge; l jisr sedd = bridge blocked. ROADS infrastructure. Corpus: cr=0.67, freq=6.

3emara.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'building' (noun). 3=3ayn digit. 3emara 2adime = old building (structural risk). SAFETY/ROADS. Corpus: cr=0.29, freq=14.

mustashfa.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'hospital' (noun). Road-to-hospital blocked; ambulance access issues. SAFETY sector. Corpus: cr=0.36, freq=25.

sayyara.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'car/vehicle' (noun). Common in road-condition and accident context. Corpus: cr=0.08, freq=39.

azme.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'crisis' (noun). hal azme = this crisis; 2azme is Arabizi digit form (2=glottal). Civic discourse noun. Corpus: cr=0.59, freq=22.

fasad.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'corruption' (noun). Civic accountability / protest context. must_not_auto_promote=true — needs sector context to avoid false positives. Corpus: cr=0.39, freq=14.

dawle.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'government/state' (noun). l dawle ma btiji = the government doesn't come. hkoume/hukume are colloquial government variants. must_not_auto_promote=true. Corpus: cr=0.25, freq=20.

2anoun.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'law' (noun). 2=glottal stop. Civic accountability discourse: fi 2anoun? = is there a law? Corpus: cr=0.20, freq=94.

7o2oq.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'rights' (pl. noun). 7=ح, 2=ق digits. wein 7o2o2na? = where are our rights? Civic demand context. Corpus: cr=0.19, freq=29.

7urriye.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'freedom' (noun). 7=ح digit. Protest / civic-rights context. Corpus: cr=0.18, freq=18.

wazara.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'ministry' (noun). Civic accountability: wazaret l ashghal = ministry of public works. Corpus: cr=0.33, freq=9.

mashroo3.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'project/plan' (noun). 3=3ayn digit. Infrastructure project discourse. Corpus: cr=0.15, freq=27.

7arb.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'war' (noun). 7=ح digit. Safety/crisis context. must_not_auto_promote=true. Corpus: cr=0.21, freq=58.

jaysh.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'army' (noun). Civic safety context. must_not_auto_promote=true. Corpus: cr=0.18, freq=12.

ma7kame.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'court/tribunal' (noun). 7=ح digit. Civic legal accountability context. Corpus: cr=0.29, freq=7.

mzahara.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'protest/demonstration' (noun). ithtiaj/2ihtijaj are MSA variants common in Arabizi. must_not_auto_promote=true. Corpus: cr=0.07, freq=31.

7adse.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'incident/accident' (noun). 7=ح digit. fi 7adse 3al tari2 = there's an accident on the road. Corpus: cr=0.33, freq=3.

7arr.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'hot/scorching heat' (adj/noun). 7=ح digit. Extreme heat safety context; fire adjacency. Corpus: cr=0.19, freq=38.

ossa.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'story/situation/issue' (noun). hal ossa = this situation; ossa ktire = big problem. Civic discourse. Corpus: cr=0.32, freq=68.

soura.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'picture/photo' (noun). Civic reporter: attaching evidence photo to complaint. suwar = plural. Corpus (photo+picture combined): cr=0.30, freq=229.

shefet.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'I saw / I noticed' (verb, 1sg past). Civic eyewitness marker: shefet hal 7adse = I saw this incident. Corpus: cr=0.23, freq=31.

mafroud.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'should be / supposed to' (modal). Civic demand phrasing: mafroud yiji 7ada = someone is supposed to come. Corpus: cr=0.17, freq=162.

sobe7.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'morning' (noun/adverb). Temporal marker in civic complaints (power off since morning). Corpus: cr=0.16, freq=235.

lyom.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'today' (temporal adverb). lyom = contracted Lebanese 'today'; alyom = MSA form. Temporal anchor in civic reports. Corpus: cr=0.28, freq=239.

shughel.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'work/job/function' (noun). Civic utility context: khraba ma 3am tishtaghal = electricity not working. Corpus: cr=0.23, freq=138.

befham.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'I understand / I get it' (verb, 1sg). Used in civic complaint rhetorical questions. Corpus: cr=0.24, freq=38.

ba3rif.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'I know / know' (verb). 3=3ayn digit. ma ba3rif = I don't know. Discourse marker in complaints. Corpus: cr=0.17, freq=321.

masari.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'money' (noun). fles/flis = coins/change (alt. colloquial). Economic civic context. Corpus: cr=0.17, freq=24.

7obb.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'love / like' (noun/verb). 7=ح digit. High-freq discourse in civic social media. Corpus: cr=0.11, freq=944.

7ayat.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'life' (noun). 7=ح digit. Civic discourse: 7ayatna saret sab3a = our life has become difficult. Corpus: cr=0.14, freq=302.

mdine.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'city' (noun). Location reference in civic complaints. Corpus: cr=0.13, freq=62.

ta3a.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'come! / come here' (verb, imperative). 3=3ayn digit. Civic urgency: ta3a shouf = come and see. Corpus: cr=0.14, freq=126.

day3a.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'village/town' (noun). 3=3ayn digit. belde/belda = district. Location in civic complaints. Corpus: cr=0.12, freq=17.

7arara.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'temperature/heat' (noun). 7=ح digit. darajt l7arara = the temperature degree. Civic safety: extreme-heat warnings, fire conditions. Corpus: cr=0.43, freq=86.

rotobe.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'humidity' (noun). rotobe 3aliye = high humidity. Structural damp / flooding context. Corpus: cr=0.38, freq=139.

riye7.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'wind' (noun). 7=ح digit. riye7 2awiye = strong wind. hawa = colloquial variant. SAFETY/FLOODING trigger: wind damage, flooding. Corpus: cr=0.35, freq=153.

3aasfe.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'storm/gale' (noun). 3=3ayn digit. 3aasfe jayye = storm coming. SAFETY/FLOODING trigger. Corpus note: cr=0.0 (weather-account tweets; word is genuine). freq=12.

8ayem.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'cloudy' (adj). 8=غ digit. Flooding precursor. 3im is alt digit rendering. must_not_auto_promote=true — weather-account-heavy signal. Corpus: cr=0.41, freq=85.

shamse.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'sun/sunny' (noun/adj). mshammas = sunny (adj form). Weather context. Corpus: cr=0.62, freq=23.

dabab.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'fog' (noun). 7abab is variant (7=ح). SAFETY/ROADS: fog reduces visibility. Corpus: cr=0.25, freq=4.

mfarre2.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'scattered/spread out/dispersed' (adj). 2=glottal digit. Weather: rain scattered; civic: scattered damage. Corpus: cr=1.0, freq=6.

tawa2o3.notes: Lebanese Arabizi: 'forecast/prediction' (noun). 2=glottal, 3=3ayn digits. taqaqqo3 = anticipation variant. Weather forecast context. Corpus: cr=1.0, freq=36.

stoplist_notes.miye: WRONG_FORM — use may (standard Lebanese Arabizi for water)
stoplist_notes.tire2: WRONG_FORM — use tari2 (standard Lebanese Arabizi for road)
stoplist_notes.khafer: NON_WORD — does not exist in Lebanese Arabic; use ri7a besh3a / ri7a mish taybe
